evidence.excerpt:
observe that checks built
to evaluate proposals as a whole can point to
claim-level prior art only by rejecting the whole
proposal. We therefore introduce CLAIMNOV,
a fine-grained, interpretable claim-level nov-
elty module. CLAIMNOVcatches 97% of dis-
guised papers at a 1.5% false-alarm rate, and
its claim-level novelty profile cuts the LLM
judge's false alarms from 11.8% to 1.5%. Be-
cause its verdict rests on claim-level evidence,
CLAIMNOValso keeps proposals that build
on established contributions, rejecting only 3%
of ICLR-accepted proposals with a reviewer-
disputed contribution and keeping 91 of 100
novel proposals with one spliced prior con-
tribution, against 76 for the strongest exist-
ing check. Code and data are available at
https://github.com/emmatliu/claimnov.

evidence.excerpt:
We introduce CLAIMNOV, an interpretable, claim-
level novelty module for research proposals that
can be dropped directly into any AI for scientific
discovery pipeline with a novelty check. As shown
in Figure 2, CLAIMNOVextracts typed claims
from research proposals, retrieves relevant same-
dimension claims from a pool of claims extracted
from prior art, scores the entailment per extracted
claim, aggregates into a novelty score, and passes
the full claim profile to a verdict judge for a binary
novel or non-novel decision. For validation experi-
ments, see Appendix O, and for exact prompts, see
Appendix C.

evidence.excerpt:
During the claim extraction stage, CLAIMNOV
takes the title and description from the research
proposal P and produces, with an LLM (gpt-4o-
mini set to temperature 0), a list of contribution
claimsC P ={c 1, . . . , cm}.
Each claim ci is typed with a dimension dc and
an attribute-value pair (ca, cv). Dimensions are
drawn from {Problem, Methodology, Resource,
Result}, while an attribute represents the axis along
which two works can be compared. For instance,
for a Result claim, the attribute may be classifica-
tion accuracy on CIFAR-10, and the value may be
an improvement from 30.1% to 76.9%. We aim to
extract a small number of claims per proposal (2.4–
2.7 on average, the prompt allowing 1–4), based
on conventions in AI research. We process each
paper in the reference pool Π through this stage
once, using its abstract as the description text, to
produce pool claimsC Π.

evidence.excerpt:
During the claim retrieval stage, CLAIMNOVtakes
a claim c from the previous stage's list of claims,
embeds its text together with its paper's title with
text-embedding-3-large, and produces a set of
relevant pool claims R(c) for comparison to that
claim.
To obtain such a set, we retrieve the k-nearest
(by cosine similarity) pool claims of the same di-
mension, keeping at most one claim per pool paper.
We determine k by pool size, taking k=10 as the
minimum based on an independent retrieval valida-
tion (see Appendix O), and for larger pools we use
the heuristic k= 0.2n d, where nd is the number of
pool papers with a claim in that dimension, capped
at 40. This gives k=10 for the disguise pools and
k≈35for the anchor pools (§4.4).

evidence.excerpt:
During the claim entailment stage, CLAIMNOV
judges the entailment of every pair (c, c′) for c′ ∈
R(c) with an LLM (gpt-4o-mini at temperature
0), giving titles and abstracts of pool papers as
context.
The judge rates the extent to which the pool
claim entails or covers the proposal claim on an
ordinal scale ℓ(c, c′)∈ {1, . . . ,5}: 1 unrelated, 2
shared topic only, 3 partial coverage with impor-
tant details differing, 4 strong coverage with minor
details missing, and 5 full coverage of the claim's
substantive content. We map these levels onto the
unit interval by taking e(c, c′) = (ℓ(c, c′)−1)/4∈
[0,1].

Finally, the novelty verdict stage of CLAIMNOV
assembles previous evidence produced by the mod-
ule into a profile Φ(P) which is evaluated by a
stronger judge (claude-sonnet-4-6). Φ(P) lists
the proposal's extracted claims with matched prior
claims, their sources (and their abstracts), and the
entailment levels.
From the judge, we receive a verdict of pass or
fail. If the proposal fails, CLAIMNOValso outputs
the prior art paper p∗ ∈Π , its subset of claims
S⊆C P , and a one- or two-sentence reason. For
the exact prompt, please see Appendix C.

evidence.excerpt:
Because six of the seven novelty checks we eval-
uate use an LLM as a judge at some point (and
CLAIMNOValso does so), we fix a cutoff T=
March 2026 and exclusively evaluate models with
earlier cutoffs. This mitigates the risk of mod-
els recognizing post-T papers from training data.
We run each check with Sonnet 4.6 (training
cutoff January 2026), which is the same model
CLAIMNOVuses as the final verdict judge (for ear-
lier, lightweight stages, CLAIMNOVuses gpt-4o-
mini). As we explain in more detail in §4.4, we
use Sonnet 4.6 to generate ideas, disguise existing
papers, and rewrite disputed papers as research pro-
posals, and Opus 4.6 (training cutoff August 2025)
as the labeler.

CLAIMNOVand CoI-Agent also reject a large share
of ideas the field went on to publish. Si et al. rejects
96%, ResearchAgent 98.5%, AI Scientist v1 52%,

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Ground truth is anchored in publication timelines, reviewer-attributed prior art, and multi-annotator human audits, with cross-family labeler checks and repeated runs.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are reported on larger held-out datasets: 380 disguised proposals, 400 later-realized ideas, 160 claim-disputed proposals, and 100 hybrid proposals.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: System prompts, dimension weights, retrieval depth, and decision thresholds were tuned on small pilot subsets, including 20 disputed pairs, 32 decoys, and a 20-paper extraction ground truth.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Claims that whole-proposal checks suffer high false-alarm rates or reject incremental work while CLAIMNOV preserves partially novel ideas and achieves higher informedness (J=0.95 vs CoI-Agent's 0.93) are well-supported by empirical data.
primary.evaluation_assessment: The evaluation thoroughly compares CLAIMNOV against seven existing novelty checks across proposal catch rates, false alarm rates, and claim-level attribution accuracy. Extensive ablations, cross-family judge checks, and human verification audits substantiate the quantitative findings.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: Evaluation uses objective ground-truth constructions (ICML/NeurIPS publication timelines, verified ICLR review disputes, and multi-annotator human validation audits).
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Headline outcomes are established on large held-out benchmark datasets (380 disguised proposals, 400 later-realized proposals, 160 reviewer disputes, and 100 hybrid spliced proposals).
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: System prompts and heuristic thresholds were calibrated using pilot subsets (such as 20 disputed pairs and 32 decoys) and GEPA prompt tuning on a small extraction dataset.

primary.limitations: The authors clearly delineate limitations, including reliance on fixed-pool retrieval rather than live web search, domain restriction to AI research, heuristics in dimension weighting, and the eventual decay of temporal cutoffs.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology decomposes research proposals into typed claims, retrieves same-dimension prior art claims, computes graded entailment, and aggregates them into a structured novelty profile evaluated by a verdict judge. The evaluation framework establishes temporal ground truth via disguised post-cutoff papers, historical ICLR reviewer disputes, and post-cutoff later-realized ideas.
primary.quality_rationale: The work addresses an important failure mode in autonomous scientific discovery pipelines with sound methodology, comprehensive benchmarking, robust statistical comparisons, and solid empirical grounding.
primary.scoped_contribution: The paper introduces an evaluation framework with temporal ground truth (1,060 proposals) for scientific novelty checking in AI pipelines, audits seven existing systems, and proposes CLAIMNOV, a claim-level novelty module.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The work addresses an important failure mode in autonomous scientific discovery pipelines with sound methodology, comprehensive benchmarking, robust statistical comparisons, and solid empirical grounding.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors clearly delineate limitations, including reliance on fixed-pool retrieval rather than live web search, domain restriction to AI research, heuristics in dimension weighting, and the eventual decay of temporal cutoffs.

limitations_or_uncertainty.value: Structured research-card claims use title, abstract/summary, metadata, screening rules, and curation. A separate scholarly-quality assessment used bounded full-text excerpts, but unsupported claim, method, or evidence fields remain unextracted.

research_relevance.value: Directly relevant to autonomous/deep research workflows based on screening evidence.
